First, we need to find the complementary function ${y}_{c}(x),$ which is the solution to the homogeneous equation

$$
{y}^{″}-5{y}^{′}+6y=0.
$$

Writing down and solving the auxiliary equation gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{\lambda }^{2}-5\lambda +6 & =0 \\ (\lambda -2)(\lambda -3) & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

So $\lambda =2$ or $\lambda =3$, and therefore the complementary function ${y}_{c}$ is

$$
y=A{e}^{2x}+B{e}^{3x}.
$$

We now need to find the particular integral ${y}_{p}(x).$

The right-hand side of the inhomogeneous equation is a polynomial of degree $1.$ Therefore, we assume that the particular integral is also a polynomial of degree $1,$ i.e.

$$
{y}_{p}(x)=\alpha x+\beta 
$$

where $\alpha $ and $\beta $ are constants that are to be determined. 

Calculating the first and second derivatives of ${y}_{p}$ gives

$$
{y}_{p}^{′}=\alpha ,\,{y}_{p}^{″}=0.
$$

To find the values of $\alpha $ and $\beta ,$ we substitute the derivatives into the differential equation:

$$
0-5\alpha +6(\alpha x+\beta )=18x+3
$$

Grouping the terms on the left-hand side gives

$$
6\alpha x+(-5\alpha +6\beta )=18x+3.
$$

Equating the coefficients, we get the following system of equations:

$$
\begin{aligned}\{\begin{aligned}6\alpha =18\, & (\text{equating the coefficients of}\,\,x) \\ -5\alpha +6\beta =3\, & (\text{equating the constants})\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Solving this system gives $\alpha =3,\beta =3.$

Therefore, the particular integral ${y}_{p}(x)$ is

$$
{y}_{p}(x)=3x+3.
$$

The general solution is given by

$$
y(x)={y}_{c}(x)+{y}_{p}(x),
$$

and therefore, the general solution in our case is

$$
y=A{e}^{2x}+B{e}^{3x}+3x+3.
$$

Now let's find the constants $A$ and $B.$ 

Substituting $y(0)=3$ into the general solution gives

$$
A+B=0.
$$

We now need to apply the condition ${y}^{′}(0)=0.$ First, we differentiate $y$ to find ${y}^{′}:$

$$
{y}^{′}=2A{e}^{2x}+3B{e}^{3x}+3
$$

Substituting ${y}^{′}(0)=0$ into the above gives

$$
2A+3B+3=0.
$$

Therefore, we have the following system of equations for $A$ and $B:$

$$
\{\begin{aligned}A+B=0 \\ 2A+3B+3=0\end{aligned}
$$

Solving this system gives $A=3,B=-3.$

Therefore, the solution to the initial value problem is

$$
y=3{e}^{2x}-3{e}^{3x}+3x+3.
$$
